description: Secondary (media) sources relied on by published Continuum notes. Maintained by scripts/archive-sources.mjs. Read at build time by content/sources/media.ts; a note citing a record whose status is not VERIFIED will not build.

sources.headline: Health insurers disallowed claims worth Rs 15,100 cr during FY24: Irdai

claimsUsed.claim: ₹15,100 crore disallowed, described as 12.9 per cent of the total claims filed
claimsUsed.excerpt: Health insurers disallowed claims worth Rs 15,100 crore or 12.9 per cent of the total claims filed during fiscal 2023-24

claimsUsed.claim: IRDAI's cashless sentence carried as written: 66.16 per cent by number cashless, another 39 per cent reimbursement
claimsUsed.excerpt: 66.16 per cent of total number of claims were settled through cashless mode and another 39 per cent through reimbursement mode

sources.headline: Health insurance claims rejection up 19.10% in FY24: Irdai report

claimsUsed.claim: ₹26,000 crore disallowed and repudiated, up 19.10 per cent
claimsUsed.excerpt: Health policy claims worth Rs 26,000 crore were disallowed and "repudiated" by insurers in the year ending March 2024, marking a 19.10 per cent increase

claimsUsed.claim: Prior-year base of ₹21,861 crore, attributed by the outlet to IRDAI
claimsUsed.excerpt: The rejection amount was Rs 21,861 crore in the year ending March 2023

claimsUsed.claim: A disallowed claim is one an insurer refuses to process over its validity
claimsUsed.excerpt: refuses to process it due to specific issues with its validity

claimsUsed.claim: Insurers rejected 11 per cent of health claims
claimsUsed.excerpt: rejected 11 per cent of health claims and had 6 per cent pending as of March 2024

claimsUsed.claim: The outlet's definition of a settlement ratio
claimsUsed.excerpt: claims an insurance company settles within a specific period

claimsUsed.claim: Public sector insurers had a settlement ratio of 103.38 per cent, read as paying out more than premiums collected
claimsUsed.excerpt: Public sector insurers had a settlement ratio of 103.38 per cent in 2023-24, indicating that they paid out more than they collected in premiums
